ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) USE POLICY (REVISED 2025)

Artificial intelligence (AI) tools may be used to support student learning when their use is appropriate for the assignment or activity. AI should support, not replace, a student's own learning, critical thinking and communication.

Appropriate uses of AI may include brainstorming, clarifying concepts, creating study materials, generating practice questions or receiving feedback when permitted by the teacher or course.

Students may not use AI to generate graded work and submit that work as their own unless the teacher or course instructions specifically permit the use of AI for that assignment.

Students are responsible for the work they submit and must be able to independently explain and demonstrate their understanding of submitted work.

When the authenticity of submitted work cannot reasonably be verified, the teacher may require the student to participate in a discussion-based assessment or other method of verification. Verification may include a live, camera-enabled session.

Work determined to be inauthentic may be subject to resubmission requirements and academic consequences in accordance with Texas Tech K-12 policy.

**Texas Tech K-12 Homeschool Curriculum and Academic Support for 12th Grade**

**Homeschool Curriculum for 12th Grade**
- Texas Tech K-12 offers a Supplemental Individual Student (Part-Time) program that is designed for students, including homeschoolers, who want to supplement their current curriculum.
- The program allows students in elementary, middle, and high school (including 12th grade) to enroll in individual courses at their own pace.
- Courses are self-paced, reading and writing intensive, and provide all instructional content online.
- Students can take courses to graduate early or on time, make up failed credits, or take courses not offered locally.
- More than 150 online courses are available, including core subjects, electives, Advanced Placement (AP), and dual credit options.

**Academic Support**
- Texas Tech K-12 provides access to certified teachers who grade assignments, provide feedback, and are available for questions via course messaging.
- Students receive progress reports and can print grade reports for completed courses.
- Homeschool students may use Texas Tech K-12 courses to establish credit or grade placement if transferring into a school.
- Academic advisors are available to assist with course selection and planning.

**Enrollment and Requirements**
- Open enrollment: Students can enroll at any time and have six months (180 days) to complete each course.
- Homeschool students should coordinate with their local school or Texas Tech K-12 advisor to ensure courses meet their academic needs.
- Most courses do not require separate textbooks; if required, information is provided in the course.

**Next Steps**
- View the course catalog and enroll online: [Texas Tech K-12 Course Catalog](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/support/coursedescriptions.php)
- For questions or personalized support, contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Texas Tech K-12 Tuition-Free Program Overview**

**Program Description:**
- Texas Tech K-12 offers a tuition-free, full-time online academic program for eligible Texas residents in grades K–12.
- The program is funded by the State of Texas and provides a flexible, accredited education that meets Texas public school standards.

**Eligibility Requirements:**
- Must be a Texas resident under the age of 25.
- Must provide proof of Texas residency (such as a current deed, lease, mortgage statement, utility bill, military documents, or a letter from the Texas Juvenile Justice Department).
- Must provide a copy of the student’s birth certificate.
- Must withdraw from your local school district to attend full-time.
- Must be scheduled into at least four semester courses and maintain satisfactory course progress.
- Must participate in required State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR) and End of Course (EOC) exams.
- Must have access to a computer that meets minimum technology requirements and reliable internet access.
- A designated Learning Coach (parent/guardian or another responsible adult) is required to help monitor progress.

**Enrollment Process:**
- Admission is limited and determined by a lottery system each semester when applications exceed available capacity.
- The next lottery for mid-year transfer is scheduled for October 29, 2026, for the 2026–2027 school year.
- Enrollment for the first semester opens August 3, 2026, and courses must be completed by January 15, 2027.
- Second semester enrollments for new students open January 4, 2027, with courses to be completed by June 30, 2027.

**Attendance & Progress Requirements:**
- Students must be enrolled in a minimum of four courses at all times.
- Attendance is measured by progress: students must complete at least 5% of course assignments every seven days and work in each course at least three days per week.
- All courses must be completed within six months of enrollment; extensions are not allowed.
- Failure to meet progress or attendance requirements may result in removal from the program.

**State Testing:**
- Participation in STAAR/EOC exams is mandatory for continued enrollment and graduation.
- Students who do not participate in required state testing will be moved to the tuition-paid program.

**What’s Provided:**
- Free online course enrollments.
- Free registration.
- Free access to required online textbooks.

**What Families Provide:**
- Student computer and reliable high-speed internet.
- General school supplies and, for some courses, household or specialty items.
- Graphing calculator for certain math courses.

**How to Apply:**
- Complete the [Texas Tech K-12 Intake Form](https://ttu.focusschoolsoftware.com/focus/apply/?_gl=1*v05loa*_gcl_au*NTY5NzA2ODU2LjE3MzA4NDA5OTY.*_ga*MjU0NDE2Nzg2LjE3MjMwNDQ2MTA.*_ga_TSPQSJQPQF*MTczMzI2MjA5Ni4xNzkuMS4xNzMzMjYyMTA1LjAuMC4w).
- Submit all required documentation (birth certificate, proof of residency, etc.).
- Applications are evaluated for lottery placement; you will be notified of your status via email.

**More Information & Support:**
- [Tuition-Free Program Details](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/freetuition/)
- Contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu

If you have additional questions or need help with the application, please reach out to the support team using the contact information above.

**How Credits Work at Texas Tech K-12**

**High School Credits:**
- Texas Tech K-12 high school courses are aligned with Texas graduation requirements.
- Each full-year course is typically worth 1 credit (0.5 credit per semester).
- To graduate, students must complete the required number of credits in core subjects and electives according to their graduation plan (e.g., Foundation Graduation Plan with Endorsement requires 26 credits).

**Credit by Exam (CBE):**
- Students can earn credit for a course by passing a Credit by Exam (CBE) instead of completing the full course.
- CBEs are available for elementary, middle, and high school subjects.
- Passing scores:
  - **Without prior instruction:** 80% or higher required to earn credit.
  - **With prior instruction:** 70% or higher required to earn credit.
- Students may attempt a CBE for the same high school course a maximum of two times (Set 1 and Set 2).

**Transferring Credits:**
- Credits from accredited public or private schools can be transferred and applied toward graduation requirements.
- Homeschool or non-accredited school credits require placement assessments or CBEs for credit validation.

**Course Completion and Credit:**
- Students must complete all assignments and the final exam to earn credit for a course.
- A passing course grade is 70% or higher.
- Only completed courses are officially reported and recorded on the transcript.

**Dual Credit:**
- Eligible high school students can earn both high school and college credit by taking approved dual credit courses through Texas Tech University.
- Dual credit courses count toward both high school graduation and college transcripts.

**Credit Recovery and Acceleration:**
- Students can retake courses or use CBEs to recover lost credits or accelerate their academic progress.

**Important Notes:**
- Course credit is only awarded after successful completion and demonstration of mastery.
- No partial credit is granted; the entire course or CBE must be completed and passed.
- Students must confirm with their school counselor or Texas Tech K-12 advisor that credits will meet their academic or graduation requirements before enrolling.
